source: Chapter VI screenplay and canonical storyboard; F01 through F04 each generated and reviewed in a separate author turn

scenes.focus: one miniature enclosed railway freight wagon is positioned by a dark-gloved investigator's hand on a weathered railway route drawing with three distinct marked locations, visually comparing known observations with an unresolved branch
scenes.camera: tight angled overhead shot of the paper rail plan on a detective's wooden table, with the one wagon token and three marked locations in sharp focus, face of the investigator completely unseen
scenes.location: a rain-shadowed private detective's office in industrial Birmingham in the 1920s
required: exactly one small dark brass freight-wagon model held between gloved fingers on the paper route
a single hand-drawn rail map with three distinct circular stop marks connected by one branching railway line, two checked points and one uncertain mark
a metal engineer's ruler and a plain mechanical drafting pen near the bottom of the map
scenes.background: old wooden worktable, worn railway ledgers, cast-metal desk lamp and rain-streaked window with distant smoke-blackened brick mills
scenes.light: focused warm amber desk-lamp illumination across aged paper and dark gloves against cool blue rainy industrial dusk
scenes.npc: one anonymous investigator visible only by dark wool sleeves and black leather gloves, no face and no other people
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The map distinguishes recorded observations from assumptions. Only one wagon and one rail journey exist. The image never proves disappearance, witness movements, a final wagon location, or completion of the investigation.
avoid: multiple wagons, a train arriving at a documented destination, or witnesses physically appearing on the map
a stamped official declaration that the wagon disappeared or reached a secret station
recognizable face or altered canonical appearance of any selectable hero
readable invented station names, routes, times, or new witness addresses

scenes.focus: an anonymous gloved investigator compares two separate old freight documents, one with flowing cursive and a light seal, the other with a tightly ruled arrival ledger and a different official seal, without joining the pages together
scenes.camera: an oblique close overhead view across a dark desk, both weathered sheets held separately in each gloved hand with the center gap clearly visible, face of the investigator fully out of frame
scenes.location: the rain-facing worktable of a modest railway investigator in industrial Birmingham during the 1920s
required: one aged left-hand freight paper dominated by flowing cursive pen strokes and a low round stamp
one separate right-hand train arrival ledger sheet dominated by tight ruled columns, a different script and its own stamp impression
two black-gloved hands keeping both paper sheets physically separate above a scratched oak table
scenes.background: a heavy brass oil desk lamp, old ink bottle, magnifying glass, closed railway ledger and a rain-wet window overlooking smoke-belching brick factories
scenes.light: an intense warm amber desk lamp across the two independent papers, contrasting with the cold blue industrial rain beyond the window
scenes.npc: only the investigator's black leather gloves and dark sleeves appear; no identifiable face or other human figures
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: These are two independent suspected falsifications, not one merged forged document. The image does not prove either account false, confirm a second forgery, establish which witness signed, reveal the whereabouts of the wagon, or identify a culprit.
avoid: readable invented signatures, witness names, fabricated station names, amounts or dates
one single joint forged sheet replacing the two materially distinct documents
an official verdict, celebratory conclusion, verified guilty party or definitive forensic proof
recognizable face or altered canonical appearance of any selectable investigator

scenes.focus: the black-gloved hand of an investigator uses metal tweezers to examine a ragged dark wool coat fiber over a shallow evidence tray, beside an old police accident report and two separate telegram and witness-account papers
scenes.camera: tight angled close-up from desk height, cropped to the hand, frayed textile fragment, evidence tray and old documents, with all human faces out of frame
scenes.location: a small police evidence and records desk beside the railway district in 1920s industrial Birmingham
required: a single frayed dark wool fabric fragment gently gripped in narrow metal tweezers above a worn metal evidence tray
one aged police accident report on a leather writing board physically separate from the evidence tray
one folded telegram form beside another handwritten account sheet, both illegible, on scratched oak
scenes.background: a dark wooden police records counter with old filing cabinets, a closed ledger and the edge of a heavy shaded lamp
scenes.light: warm amber lamplight emphasizing torn fabric strands and paper edges, with cooler rainy urban light beyond the desk
scenes.npc: only one black-gloved investigator's hand and part of a dark wool coat are visible, without any identifiable face
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The scene juxtaposes conflicting clues about Hale's death; the police accident report remains an earlier claim. The image cannot independently set provedHaleMurder, establish a suspect, or decide whether the death was criminal.
avoid: depicting Hale alive, a body, a reenacted attack, a murderer, or a decisive confession
an official proven-homicide ruling, a named suspect or concluded investigation
readable witness names, telegram destinations, detailed fabricated forensic findings, or signatures
an identifiable selectable hero's face or an unauthorized replacement portrait

scenes.focus: a detective's black-gloved index finger pauses beside the sixth entry in a battered factory ledger, comparing its six separate numbered lines with a distinct official registry sheet bearing only two numbered handwritten entries
scenes.camera: moderately elevated three-quarter close shot diagonally across the factory archive desk, emphasizing the distinct two-line official paper on the left and the longer six-line open ledger on the right
scenes.location: a dusty factory record-keeping room in Birmingham in the 1920s
required: one small aged official-looking sheet with only two handwritten numbered entries and an old ink seal, resting by itself to the left
one open thick worn bound factory register displaying precisely six individually numbered entries in one column
one anonymous investigator's black leather gloved forefinger indicating the lowest sixth ledger line while keeping all character faces outside the frame
scenes.background: weathered factory filing cabinets, tied paper bundles, an old clerk's ink-stamp press, a scratched dark oak table and a large window overlooking smoking industrial chimneys
scenes.light: dry soft grey industrial daylight across the two lists with a restrained warm reflection off faded brown paper and dark polished wood
scenes.npc: only the unseen investigator's hand and dark wool sleeve enter the frame; no visible faces or other people
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The discrepancy between two official entries and six factory ledger entries is only a comparison. The image does not establish provedFactoryCoverup, verified wrongdoing, a court judgment, or a legally confirmed list of implicated people.
avoid: legible or invented surnames, dates, addresses, witness identities, or additional names
a seventh person, extra numbered ledger entry, or more than two entries on the official notice
a guilty verdict, signed confession, celebratory discovery, or certified conclusion
an identifiable selectable hero's face or a replacement portrait of a known character
